title: Grateful Dead Live at Dillon Stadium on 1972-07-16
lineage: source 1: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC> SHN; source 2: AUD> ?> SHN

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording with mixed sound quality captures a legendary Allman‑Dead jam and Dickey Betts guests, delivering a hot, high‑energy set.
ai_review.review: The show is celebrated for its explosive second‑set jams – especially the NFA > Good Lovin' > Hey Bo Diddley sequence, the massive Truckin’ → The Other One stretch and the first ever performance of “Mississippi Half‑Step Uptown Toodleloo.”  While the soundboard portions are solid, the audience tracks are hissy and uneven, giving the recording a fair overall fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (high‑energy jams, special guests) despite noting mixed technical quality; weighted average of show (~4.5) and recording (~3.0) yields ~4.1.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Soundboard sections are decent but contain hiss; audience portions are low‑fidelity, especially early tracks. Mix is uneven – Phil’s bass and Keith’s keyboards sometimes overpower other instruments.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑part show with a strong first set, an epic second set jammed with Allman Brothers guests, and a memorable encore; the flow builds to a fiery climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Ripping leads like a madman; notable call‑and‑response with Dickey Betts during the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is massive and pushed forward in the mix, especially on the Allman jam sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are very high in the mix to the point of distortion on some tracks.
